hypothesis: Beneficial-versus-harmful action status is separable from label-blind global assignment sensitivity even when local endpoint appearance is not.

c0_assignment.baseline_state: The pinned APNCC graph is the explicit no-op state.
c0_assignment.action_cost: Negative authenticated Trackastra challenger-minus-incumbent margin, exactly b0[:,48], float64.
c0_assignment.component: Transitive closure over source outgoing boundary, destination incoming boundary, every incumbent edge removed, challenger edge, and explicit no-op endpoint.
c0_assignment.feasible_assignment: Any pairwise ownership-disjoint subset of candidate actions, including the empty subset. Frozen N1 witness construction establishes each action; the pinned structural execution checked all batches requiring C2 adjudication and observed 361 accepts / 0 rejects.
c0_assignment.map: Minimum math.fsum float64 action cost; ties by lexicographically sorted tuples of canonical N1 action SHA-256 values.
c0_assignment.k_best: The first min(8, number of distinct feasible assignments) assignments in the same total-cost/canonical-tuple order. No padding or invented assignment is allowed.
c0_assignment.delete_event: For frozen baseline edge e, applying the delete action is the binary event that at least one selected occupied-swap action owns and removes e. If no candidate action can remove e, force-in is structurally infeasible.
c0_assignment.occupied_swap_event: Applying the swap action is the binary event that its candidate action belongs to the assignment.
c0_assignment.infeasible_force_sentinel: For a structurally infeasible event only, set force-in regret to M=1+sum(abs(component action costs)), forbid regret to 0, and signed min-marginal to M. This fixed structural sentinel is selected without labels.
c0_assignment.transfer_domain: Murty/Lawler justify ordered feasible-assignment enumeration. Exact binary-event min-marginals are a MAP sensitivity diagnostic. Neither literature source validates the G-02 costs, cell-tracking labels, or graph gain; those remain empirical.

supplier_features.dtype: float32 output derived from deterministic float64 solves

definitions.event_in_c0_map: 1 iff the class-specific edit event occurs in the C0 MAP assignment.
definitions.force_in_regret: C_include(event)-C_best, or the frozen infeasible-force sentinel.
definitions.signed_min_marginal_c_in_minus_c_out: C_include(event)-C_exclude(event); this is the exact binary-event reduced-cost/regret, negative when applying the edit is preferred.
definitions.kbest_membership_fraction: Unweighted event membership among K_eff=min(8, feasible assignment count).
definitions.kbest_rank_weighted_membership: Event membership weighted K_eff,K_eff-1,...,1 and divided by K_eff*(K_eff+1)/2.
definitions.log1p_component_action_count: Natural log of one plus the number of candidate actions in the complete assignment component.
definitions.log1p_local_competitor_count: Natural log of one plus the number of other component actions sharing any owned primitive with the swap; for delete, the number of candidate actions capable of removing its incumbent edge.

forbidden: oracle label or oracle delta in feature generation

alignment_control.rule: Within each action class, video, and source frame, sort row identities by SHA-256 of the frozen seed and canonical row identity, then cyclically shift A1 feature rows by one. Strata of size one remain fixed.

feasibility_and_sampling.delete_attachment: One streaming edge-to-component lookup over 1,345,497 frozen delete rows.
feasibility_and_sampling.reason: Exact enumeration is bounded by tiny independent components; full delete attachment is linear and requires no model forward pass.

gate.probe: Unchanged class-balanced standardized ridge least-squares binary rank probe, lambda 0.01, deterministic float64.

barrier.pass: Unlock only a supplier-specific 44b6 graph-gate preregistration for human review.
barrier.fail: Park that supplier x action-class instantiation PARK-C.
barrier.halt: No graph run, 6bba, CV57, GPU, submission, RunPod, tier move, or plan amendment.

literature.citation: Murty, K.G. (1968), An Algorithm for Ranking all the Assignments in Order of Increasing Cost, Operations Research 16(3):682-687.
Lawler, E.L. (1972), A Procedure for Computing the K Best Solutions to Discrete Optimization Problems and Its Application to the Shortest Path Problem, Management Science 18(7):401-405.
